To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel T854A second-site mutation in EGFR is associated with acquired resistance to EGFR kinase inhibitors.

we have identified a second site acquired resistance mutation, T854A, that is in contact with erlotinib and gefitinib and is associated with acquired resistance to erlotinib in a lung adenocarcinoam with an L858R mutation.

a novel acquired second-site mutation (T854A) in EGFR was identified in one case of acquired resistance to EGFR tyrosin kinase inhibitors and that BIBW 2929, an irreversible inhibitor of the EGFR and HER2 tyrosine kinases, overcomes resistance to erlotinib caused by the T854A mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new drugs to treat patients with lung cancer.
the identification of second site acquired resistance mutations in patients with EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
the identification of second-site acquired resistance mutations that may lead to the development of more effective EGFR kinase inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T854A mutation in EGFR is a novel acquired resistance mechanism in EGFR-mutant lung cancer.
the T854A mutation in the EGFR gene is a second site acquired resistance mutation in a patient with EGFR-mutant lung cancer after long-term treatment.
the T790M mutation is the most common acquired resistance mutation to EGFR-TKI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the EGFR-T790M mutation is the predominant acquired resistance mutation to the EGFR kinase inhibitors gefitinib and/or erlotinib, but other acquired resistance mutations, including T790M and T854A, may also be present in patients with lung adenocarcinaomas that have acquired resistance to the kinase inhibitors.
the T854A mutation in exon 20 is a novel acquired resistance mutation to gefitinib or erlotinib in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarinoma.
we found that the T854A mutation in the EGFR kinase domain is a novel acquired drug-resistance mechanism that is within contact of gefitinib, erlotinib, and other EGFR inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acquired resistance to EGFR TKIs may be associated with mutations that are within contact distance of the ATP-binding site.
we identified a novel mutation in the EGFR gene that is responsible for acquired resistance to EGFR tyrosin kinase inhibitors.

acquired resistance to the ATP-competitive EGFR kinase inhibitors, erlotinib and gefitinib, may often be associated, at least in part, with mutations that alter the drug contact residues in their ATP-binding pocket.
